## The hill gets busy

v1.5.13 built the ski hill. This one fixes what was wrong with it after
actually watching it run for a while, which is a different exercise
entirely from building it.

### The gondolas are gone

They were tried at two sizes and both were wrong. Small, they were a row
of lit rectangles sliding across the sky and the only thing they said was
"lit rectangle". Big enough to see inside — with passengers, a dog, and
occasionally the yeti riding up for another go — they read as a
completely separate scene happening *above* the hill rather than as part
of it.

The underlying problem is that a gondola crosses horizontally and the
entire subject of this screen is a slope running the other way. Nothing
about the size was ever going to fix that. The sky keeps the moon, the
stars, the cloud banks and the satellite, and it is better for it.

### Three riders, and some of them are on boards

There is no longer *a* skier. There are **three riders on the hill, each
on their own timer**, and each one re-rolls what they are riding every
time they drop in — roughly forty percent snowboards.

The snowboarder is a deliberately different silhouette rather than a
recoloured skier: one plank instead of two, a wide stance with the
shoulders square across the hill instead of pointed down it, no poles, a
beanie instead of a bobble hat. He gets his own tricks too — an indy
grab, a method, and a spin. Boards also run slightly slower than skis,
which is a small thing and is most of the difference between three riders
and one rider drawn three times.

**They also have different jackets.** Three outfits each, re-rolled per
run. Same silhouette, different person.

### The yeti now picks someone

This is the real fix behind all of the above. With one skier, the slope
was empty most of the time, so the yeti would decide it was time to hunt
and there would be **nobody there to hunt**. He was waiting on a target
that did not exist.

He now chooses a rider — whichever one is furthest along but still has
most of the hill left, so there is somewhere for the chase to happen. If
that rider makes it off the edge, the chase ends because the rider
genuinely got away, rather than because a timer ran out.

### They talk now

The chase comes with **speech bubbles**. The yeti announces himself, the
rider answers, and they trade lines the whole way down — alternating, so
it reads as an argument rather than two monologues. The punchline depends
on how it ended, and the loser generally says less.

### The sky stopped being stripes

The single biggest visual change in this release, and it costs almost
nothing.

This panel quantises blue to **four levels**. Not 256, not 32 — four. So
a blue gradient could be cut into eighteen bands and still only ever show
four flat steps, which is exactly why the night sky read as stripes no
matter how it was tuned.

The sky is now **dithered one row at a time**: a repeating four-row
threshold nudges alternate rows either side of the quantisation boundary
so the eye mixes them. Roughly thirteen apparent shades out of four real
ones, for an identical pixel count.

### A moon you can look at

Redrawn at nearly twice the diameter with actual **maria** — big soft
dark seas, overlapping so the edges are irregular rather than three
obvious circles — and **five craters, each with a lit rim on the sunward
side**, which is what makes a disc read as cratered rather than as a
blotchy circle. Limb shading down the trailing edge finishes it as a
sphere.

The old glow is gone. It was three rings blended toward a single sampled
sky colour, and since a glow spans about fifty rows of a vertical
gradient, it was too dark at one end and too light at the other — it read
as a hole cut in the sky rather than as light.

### Trees that look like trees

The pines were a striped triangle. Two changes fixed it, and neither was
"add more rows".

First, the rows **do not taper cleanly** any more — the little jumps back
out are branch tips catching light, and a perfectly monotonic taper is
what made them read as stripes in the first place. Second, the shading
now runs **across** the tree rather than down it. Banding by row is what
the eye reads as stripes; banding by side is what it reads as a lit
object. The moon sits low on the left, so the left face is lit.

Snow sits on the branch tops in three short broken runs rather than one
even bar, for the same reason: a long unbroken run is the same mistake in
a lighter colour.

### Two things you asked about

**No more pink snow.** The far ridge was blending most of the way toward
the sky colour, which is unobjectionable at night and turned the entire
far slope pink the moment dawn warmed the horizon. Snow takes a little of
the light; it does not become the light.

**One pixel of air above the counters.** The background floor now stops
a pixel short. "ACTIVE DETECTIONS" survives on any background because it
is drawn with a black outline first — but the counter numbers underneath
are plain text with no outline, and cyan on white snow is the one
combination on this device that genuinely cannot be read.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: snowboarders, with their own silhouette and their own tricks
- **Added**: three riders on the hill at once, mixed skis and boards, each with their own outfit
- **Added**: speech bubbles — the yeti and the riders trash talk through the whole chase
- **Changed**: the gondola line has been removed entirely
- **Fixed**: the yeti used to start chases when there was nobody on the hill to chase
- **Fixed**: the sky rendered as flat stripes — it is dithered per row now
- **Fixed**: the pines rendered as a striped triangle
- **Fixed**: the far slope turned pink at dawn
- **Fixed**: the background could butt straight into the detection counters
- **Changed**: the moon is bigger, cratered, and no longer has a fake glow around it
